answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may post offers or vote. The protocol caps influence by locked stake, so splitting one deposit across a hundred identities grants no more weight than keeping one. A challenger can prove fraud and trigger slashing, while honest stake stays locked and unavailable for other uses. The haven is not anonymity: an attacker must buy or borrow capital, risk losing it, and pay the opportunity cost of tying it up across a canyon of identities in a nebula of activity.
